problem:
Find an eigenvector of 
$A=[\begin{aligned}4 & -6 \\ -6 & 4\end{aligned}]$
that corresponds to the eigenvalue $\lambda =10.$

activity_context.topic_title: Calculating the Eigenvectors of a 2x2 Matrix

examples.knowledge_point: Calculating an Eigenvector Corresponding to an Eigenvalue
examples.problem:
Find an eigenvector of ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14069178/assets/a37420b7df40cfb806fadac008680a2e7346b1b2dea5d89a4baa912ab0bedb14.png)
that corresponds to the eigenvalue $\,\lambda=2.$
examples.worked_solution:
To compute the eigenvectors of a matrix, we need to find non-zero solutions of the matrix equation 

$$
(A - \lambda I) \textbf{x}=\mathbf{0}.
$$

 

In our case, we have $\,\lambda =2.$ So, we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}A-\lambda I & =[\begin{aligned}7 & -4 \\ 5 & -2\end{aligned}]-2[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}5 & -4 \\ 5 & -4\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

We have to solve the corresponding homogeneous system of linear equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}5{x}_{1}-4{x}_{2}=0 \\ 5{x}_{1}-4{x}_{2}=0\end{aligned}
$$

So, we row-reduce the augmented matrix $M$ to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}5 & -4 & 0 \\ 5 & -4 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-1){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}5 & -4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, there is one pivot column (the $1$st one). So, $x_2$ is a free variable. 

From the first equation, we obtain 

$$
5x_1-4x_2=0
\qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad
x_1=\dfrac{4}{5}x_2.
$$

Therefore, the general solution is

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14069178/assets/65b8ab3a3e0506afb1a0c3a7a928e21b98bcda313bafcbcfdb5b02771dd91693.png)

Finally, setting $x_2=5,$ we get the eigenvector 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14069178/assets/a5098e5100bed7d15053e81b1127a774b828e30473718c6fc3fe73444eca3148.png)

feedback.problem:
If $v=[\begin{aligned}a \\ b\end{aligned}]$ is an eigenvector of 
$A=[\begin{aligned}4 & 9 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}]$
that corresponds to the eigenvalue $\lambda =7,$
then what is the value of $\frac{b}{a}?$
feedback.worked_solution:
To compute the eigenvectors of a matrix, we need to find non-zero solutions of the matrix equation 

$$
(A-\lambda I)\text{x}=0.
$$

 

In our case, we have $\,\lambda =7.$ So, we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}A-\lambda I & =[\begin{aligned}4 & 9 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}]-7[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-3 & 9 \\ 2 & -6\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have the homogeneous system of linear equations

$$
{\begin{aligned}-3{x}_{1}+9{x}_{2}=0 \\ 2{x}_{1}-6{x}_{2}=0\end{aligned}
$$

with the augmented matrix $M$ which we reduce to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}-3 & 9 & 0 \\ 2 & -6 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(\frac{2}{3}){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-3 & 9 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, there is one pivot column (the $1$st one). Thus, ${x}_{2}$ is a free variable. 

From the first equation, we obtain 

$$
-3{x}_{1}+9{x}_{2}=0\,⟹\,{x}_{1}=3{x}_{2}.
$$

Hence, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}3{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R.
$$

Setting, for instance, ${x}_{2}=1,$ we get the eigenvector 

$$
v=[\begin{aligned}a \\ b\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 1\end{aligned}]
$$

Finally, $\frac{b}{a}=\frac{1}{3}.$
